title: Pragyan Ojha Takes Interim Charge as BCCI Chief Selector After Agarkar Exit
excerpt: With Ajit Agarkar's contract expiring October 4, the BCCI asked senior-most selector Pragyan Ojha — a 24-Test veteran — to take charge; he is also a leading candidate for the permanent role.
body:
• Ajit Agarkar's tenure as BCCI chairman of selectors ended when his contract expired on October 4, and he was conspicuously absent from the selection committee's meeting with head coach Gautam Gambhir in Guwahati on September 29.
  • Former India left-arm spinner Pragyan Ojha, already a member of the four-man selection panel, was asked by the BCCI to take charge of proceedings in an interim capacity — and has emerged as a leading candidate for the permanent role.
  • Ojha, 40, played 24 Tests for India — more than fellow selectors Shiv Sunder Das (23), RP Singh (14) and Ajay Ratra (6) — taking 113 Test wickets at 30.27 across 144 international wickets.
  • The selectors will meet this week to finalize India's squads for the home tour of New Zealand — five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests from October 22 to November 27. Whoever gets the permanent job will also shape India's 2027 World Cup squad, including the question of Rohit Sharma's future.

Ajit Agarkar's time as chairman of the BCCI selection committee is over. According to a report by Cricbuzz, the former India pacer's contract expired on October 4, and his absence from a selection meeting with head coach Gautam Gambhir in Guwahati on September 29 confirmed that the transition had already begun. In his place, the BCCI has asked Pragyan Ojha — the senior-most member of the selection panel by Test appearances — to take interim charge.

"You never know anything might happen in the BCCI. But Ojha looks an acceptable candidate for everyone."

— BCCI source, via Cricbuzz

How the transition happened

The signs were visible before any announcement. Agarkar missed the Guwahati meeting on the eve of the second ODI against West Indies, where the panel — Ojha, Shiv Sunder Das, RP Singh and Ajay Ratra — held discussions with Gambhir. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia was also present and addressed the selectors on the way forward. With Agarkar's contract running out on October 4, the board opted for an interim arrangement rather than rushing a permanent appointment.

The situation, as Cricbuzz described it, remains fluid: whether Ojha continues as chairman or a new person is appointed has not been decided. Several reports in recent weeks have also linked former India wicketkeeper-batter Parthiv Patel to the role. But Ojha's position strengthened the moment he chaired the meeting in Guwahati — interim setups in Indian cricket have a habit of becoming permanent when results follow.

Ojha's credentials

Pragyan Ojha played 24 Tests, 18 ODIs and 6 T20Is for India between the late 2000s and early 2010s, finishing with 144 international wickets. Test cricket was his strongest arena — 113 wickets at an average of 30.27 as a slow left-arm orthodox spinner. His final international appearance came in 2013 at the Wankhede Stadium in the match that doubled as Sachin Tendulkar's farewell, where Ojha claimed ten wickets and was named Player of the Match. Since retiring, he has moved through broadcasting, cricket administration and — since joining the panel — national selection.

Within the current panel, Ojha's 24 Tests make him the natural internal choice. Shiv Sunder Das played 23 Tests, RP Singh 14 and Ajay Ratra six. The BCCI has traditionally valued playing experience at the top of the selection table, and Ojha's standing with the current team management appears solid.

What it means for Indian cricket

The immediate task for Ojha's panel is a big one: finalizing India's squads for the home series against New Zealand — five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests running from October 22 to November 27. That selection cycle will shape the side heading into a crowded 12 months.

The larger prize is next year. Whoever is ultimately appointed chief selector — Ojha, Parthiv Patel or an outside name — will carry the biggest responsibility in Indian selection: picking the squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup. That means answering the hardest questions in the sport — Rohit Sharma's future foremost among them — and resolving the all-rounder and fast-bowling dilemmas that have shadowed recent selections. The choice of chairman is, in effect, a bet on who Indian cricket trusts to rebuild toward 2027.

What's next

The selectors are expected to meet this week to lock in the New Zealand squads, with Ojha presiding. Whether the BCCI moves to confirm him permanently, advertises the post through the Cricket Advisory Committee process, or pivots to Parthiv Patel remains open. For now, Indian cricket's most consequential committee has a new interim head — and a decision that cannot wait much longer.
